name: Failed Discoveries That Changed Science
tagline: Serendipity, mistakes, and the surprising origin stories of breakthroughs.
seo_title: Failed Discoveries That Changed Science | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Failed Discoveries That Changed Science on LinkedIn and Facebook: stories of failed experiments, accidents and serendipity that led to breakthroughs.

definition.lead: Some of chemistry's biggest breakthroughs came from failed experiments, contaminated samples and things nobody was looking for.
definition.body: A purple dye from a failed attempt at quinine, Teflon from a gas cylinder that seemed empty, penicillin from a contaminated plate. The common thread is not luck alone, but someone who noticed something odd and asked why.

timeline.title: Vulcanized rubber
timeline.text: According to the usual account, Charles Goodyear finds that rubber heated with sulfur stays elastic after an accident on a hot stove.

timeline.title: Mauve instead of quinine
timeline.text: William Perkin's failed attempt to make quinine gives the first synthetic dye.

timeline.title: Saccharin
timeline.text: Constantin Fahlberg notices a sweet taste on his hands after a day in the lab.

timeline.title: X-rays
timeline.text: Wilhelm Röntgen notices a screen glowing across his lab while working with a cathode-ray tube.

timeline.title: Radioactivity
timeline.text: Henri Becquerel finds that uranium salts darkened plates stored in a drawer on cloudy days.
timeline.why: He expected sunlight to be needed; it was not.

timeline.title: Penicillin
timeline.text: Alexander Fleming returns from holiday to find mould killing bacteria on a culture plate.
timeline.why: The start of the antibiotic era.

timeline.title: Teflon
timeline.text: Roy Plunkett finds that a cylinder of tetrafluoroethylene gas has turned into a slippery white solid.

timeline.title: Aspartame
timeline.text: James Schlatter notices a sweet taste while working on an ulcer drug.

timeline.title: A glue that didn't stick
timeline.text: Spencer Silver at 3M makes a weak adhesive that later becomes Post-it Notes.
timeline.why: A 'failure' found its use years later.

timeline.title: Quasicrystals
timeline.text: Dan Shechtman sees a diffraction pattern that was thought impossible.
timeline.why: Rejected for years; Nobel Prize in 2011.
